report:
Reviewed the full meta.reviews.review_delegation claim, associated review.rs PROMPT implementation and the complete review_skill_assigns_one_owner_and_requires_start_read_record test. Captured and read the actual .agents/skills/sage-review-checklist/SKILL.md dependency. No behavior tests were executed; this is source inspection.

The claim is explicitly about what the repository skill instructs, not automatic spawning or enforcement of agent behavior. The coordinator section requires one review subagent per failing anchor including TODO/N/A, supplies the anchor ID with the instruction to start and inspect printed inputs, assigns one owner per validation directory while allowing concurrency across anchors, forbids uncaptured source context and saves extra coordinator instructions with start --instructions. Reviewer sections require fresh start, inspection of all initial fragments, capture of every additional source dependency with review read and completion through review record. The follow-up section assigns reconciliation/coordination to the main agent, requires fresh affected-anchor start/read/record cycles after changes and rerunning cargo meta check, and prohibits substituting a coordinator draft for a subagent's completed record. The associated PROMPT reinforces assigned-anchor scope, captured dependencies, complete reports, TODO/N/A explanation and restart after edits/staleness.

The test includes the real skill text and extracts coordinator, reviewer and follow-up role sections separately. Its normalized-whitespace assertions require each delegation/ownership/concurrency/instruction-capture obligation in the coordinator section, explicit read and record command examples in reviewer sections, and reconciliation, affected-anchor refresh and check-again instructions in the follow-up section. These are meaningful assertions for this documentary contract: they test responsible-role placement and required workflow rather than merely searching the whole file for isolated tool names. Markdown line wrapping is intentionally not semantic. There are no hidden test helpers beyond standard string operations and the captured include file.

All claim aspects are present in the skill and checked by the test or directly traced to the relevant role instructions. This review does not claim automated enforcement or that every agent execution complies solely because text exists. No associated TODO/N/A evidence, concrete defect or necessary edit was found. No source changes are requested.
